answer: An operator reserves one tagged willow coppice whose stool is locked at signup. Only that holder may hang that season's rods on a loft-numbered drying trellis and, when the mill rings an unannounced beat, watermark a single sheet with a serial-sawn opal die whose inclusion map is on file. Graders match stool tag, die inclusions, trellis number, and vat log. A shared stool, a borrowed die, or a sheet struck off-beat is merged into one farm. Fielding N aliases costs N living coppices, N distinct opal dies, and N attendants at the vat in the same beat, which one mill hand cannot cover.
